questions.question: Explain the difference between weather and climate, using Upington as an example.
questions.expected_answer: Weather is the condition of the air at a particular place and time, and it changes from day to day, such as a thunderstorm in Upington on one Wednesday. Climate is the usual pattern of weather in a place over about thirty years or more. Upington has a hot, dry climate with hot summers and little rain, so one rainy day does not give it a wet climate.

questions.question: Name the elements of weather and the instruments used to measure them.
questions.expected_answer: The elements of weather include temperature, rainfall or precipitation, wind direction and speed, cloud cover and humidity. A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius, a rain gauge measures rainfall in millimetres, a wind vane shows wind direction, and a wind sock or anemometer shows wind strength.

questions.question: Why is climate important to people, plants and animals?
questions.expected_answer: Climate decides which natural vegetation can grow in a place, and therefore which animals can live there. It affects which crops farmers can grow and whether they need irrigation, what houses people build, what clothes they wear and how they spend their time. For example, farmers near Upington irrigate grapes with water from the Orange River because the climate is too dry.
